q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a wooden chair, table or bed?
title: Wooden furniture carbon footprint per piece
short: Weigh the solid wood, plywood or MDF, adhesives, polish, hardware and packaging in one piece and apply supplier or database factors. Add kiln drying fuel, workshop electricity and finishing. Report the carbon stored in the wood separately, not as a deduction from the total.
audience: Furniture makers and exporters, including Jodhpur and Saharanpur workshops

ul: Solid wood such as sheesham, mango or acacia: count the log or sawn timber bought, including offcuts.
Plywood, MDF or particle board: resin content makes these higher per kg than solid wood.
Adhesives, polish, lacquer, PU coating and stain.
Hardware, glass, upholstery foam and fabric where used, and export cartons and foam.
Kiln or seasoning chamber fuel: often firewood or offcuts, whose CO2 is biogenic and reported separately.
Electricity for saws, planers, CNC routers, sanders and spray booths.
Compressor electricity for spray guns and nailers.

p: Wood holds carbon taken from the air. Product footprint standards ask you to report this biogenic carbon separately, not to net it off. If the timber comes from land cleared of forest, land use change emissions apply, and EU buyers may also ask for EUDR traceability.

example.title: Worked example: furniture workshop per piece (one month)
lines: Generator diesel: 600 litres x 2.68 = 1,608 kg CO2
Plant total: 10,128 / 800 = 12.66 kg CO2 per piece
Add timber, boards, finishes, hardware and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
